address: Tan Phuoc, behind Cho Thiec market, District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A signless, nearly-70-year cà phê vợt (sock-brew) stall run by ethnic-Chinese Mr Luu Nhan Thanh, who opens from ~2am and brews over a wood stove using earthenware pots once used for Chinese medicine - one of the last Hoa cà phê vợt in Saigon.

address: rooftop of the old French railway-repair factory, Cach Mang Thang 8, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A Đà Lạt-styled café built on the previously-abandoned rooftop of an early-20th-century French railway repair works; over 1,500 m2, breezy, and looking down onto working train sheds - a viral reclaimed-industrial hangout.
dish: cà phê & view (Đà Lạt-vibe rooftop over a rail factory)

address: 200 Pasteur, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A three-storey specialty roastery clad in flattened burnt-orange brick, run by a well-known Saigon barista; a serious rừng-xay bean program that drew the city's coffee community and later opened a branch in France.

address: 316 Le Van Sy, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (original Dong Khoi branch since ~1950, demolished 2010)
w: A 60-year Saigon patisserie-café brand, one of the legendary pre-1975 'Givral-Brodard-La Pagode' café axis on old Tu Do St; still famous for its bánh kem bắp (corn-cream cake).

address: 130 Tran Hung Dao, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: One of Saigon's earliest Japanese matcha houses, on busy Tran Hung Dao but kept quiet and minimalist Kyoto-style; matcha, houjicha and black-sesame drinks plus Japanese sweets.

address: upper floors off Pasteur, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A raw, bare-brick craft-beer hideout up the top floors of a crumbling old building, with 16-20 rotating taps of local craft (Pasteur Street, Heart of Darkness, Fuzzy Logic, LAC) and two rooftop terraces over the State Bank.
dish: local craft beer (16-20 rotating taps, rooftop)

address: 18 Duong So 6, Thao Dien Ward, District 2 (Thu Duc City), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A Scandinavian-meets-tropical riverside cocktail-and-dining complex in Thao Dien - terracotta walls, an open kitchen and a bar overlooking the Saigon River; a favourite sunset spot with local-fruit signature cocktails.

address: Level 23, Centec Tower, 72-74 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A long-running Mediterranean-styled rooftop lounge on the 23rd floor of Centec Tower - greenery, a glass dome and panoramic city views spanning District 1-3, with live acoustic/jazz sets and signature cocktails.

address: corner of Le Loi & Pasteur, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A legendary Saigon ice-cream parlour since 1983 at the Le Loi/Pasteur corner, tied to the childhood of generations; famed for coconut ice cream served in the shell and fresh-fruit flavours made daily.
dish: kem dừa (coconut ice cream in the shell)

address: 290/3 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia, Ward 8, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: One of Saigon's two oldest ice-cream shops, founded 1975 ('The Godfather'); a nostalgic red-and-black room hung with paintings, known for creamy coconut-milk ice cream with peach, lychee, coconut jelly and fruit cocktail.
dish: kem sữa dừa (coconut-milk ice cream, since 1975)

n: Chè Mâm Khánh Vy (Chè Năm Trăm)
address: Su Van Hanh, beside Ngo Gia Tu apartments, Ward 2, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A ~40-50-year Saigon dessert institution old-timers still call 'chè năm trăm' (500-đồng chè); it invented the 16-bowl 'chè mâm' tray - chè bà ba, chè thưng, chè chuối, chè bắp, đậu trắng, khoai môn, trôi nước plus flan and coconut jelly.

address: 504 Nguyen Kiem, Phu Nhuan District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A 40+-year pavement chè stall of ông bà Tư, lit every night since 1976 by a single oil lamp (hence the name); a wooden plank, a few plastic stools and chè at 5,000 đồng a bowl - chè chuối, trôi nước, me, bột đậu xanh, đậu trắng.

address: Tran Quoc Toan, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (est. 2005; branches citywide)
w: A first-generation Saigon milk-tea brand (since 2005) that 8x/9x locals grew up on, singled out by Thanh Nien among the city's original trà sữa shops; classic pearl, fruit-jelly and egg-flan toppings.
dish: trà sữa trân châu (original-era bubble tea)

n: Bánh Pía Triều Châu Triệu Minh Hiệp
address: 123/23 Binh Tay, Ward 1, District 6 (Cho Lon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A nearly-80-year hand-shaped Teochew (Triều Châu) bakery in Cho Lon, opened 1948 and never once moved through three generations; crisp-crust bánh pía and traditional Chaoshan candies made by hand.
dish: bánh pía Triều Châu (hand-made Teochew pastry)

address: originated on Nguyen Thien Thuat, District 3; branch at 116 Dinh Tien Hoang, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A Hoa-style herbal cooling-tea (nước sâm) name since 1977, grown from a single cart into one of Saigon's biggest nước-sâm chains; hand-brewed mía lau, bông cúc and rong biển cooling teas.

address: Cho Lon, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A century-old Cho Lon herbal-tea (trà sâm) shop, one of the oldest surviving Hoa cooling-tea houses in Saigon, kept with its old wooden carved statue; draws young visitors for Tet photos.
